metadata.description: Scenario-Based Study Guide for AIF-C01 certification - validates foundational knowledge of AI/ML concepts, AWS AI services, responsible AI practices, and the machine learning lifecycle.

questions.title: Machine Learning Definition
questions.scenario: A business executive is evaluating whether machine learning could help their company. They need to understand the fundamental concept of ML before making investment decisions.
questions.questionText: Which statement best describes machine learning?

choices.text: A subset of AI where systems learn patterns from data to make predictions without being explicitly programmed
A programming technique that uses if-then-else rules to make decisions
A method of storing and retrieving data from databases
A technique for manually coding decision logic based on expert knowledge

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about what separates learning from experience versus following hand-written rules.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence where algorithms learn patterns from data to make predictions or decisions. Unlike traditional programming where rules are explicitly coded, ML systems discover patterns in data and use them to make inferences on new, unseen data. This allows ML to handle complex problems that would be difficult to solve with hand-coded rules.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• ML algorithms improve with more data - they can discover patterns humans might miss.
  • The three main types of ML are supervised learning, unsupervised learning, and reinforcement learning.
  • Deep learning is a subset of ML using neural networks with many layers.

questions.title: Supervised vs Unsupervised Learning
questions.scenario: A data science team has a dataset of customer transactions labeled as "fraudulent" or "legitimate." They want to train a model to detect fraud in new transactions.
questions.questionText: Which type of machine learning is most appropriate for this fraud detection task?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider which approach benefits from having the correct answers already provided in the training data.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Supervised learning is the appropriate choice because the dataset includes labels (fraudulent/legitimate). The model learns the relationship between transaction features and their labels, then applies this knowledge to classify new transactions. Common supervised learning tasks include classification (categories) and regression (continuous values).

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Unsupervised learning finds patterns in unlabeled data - useful for clustering or anomaly detection when labels aren't available.
  • Reinforcement learning involves an agent learning through trial and error in an environment.
  • Semi-supervised learning uses a combination of labeled and unlabeled data.

questions.title: Deep Learning Neural Networks
questions.scenario: A company wants to build an image recognition system that can identify products from photos. They've heard that deep learning excels at image tasks.
questions.questionText: What type of neural network architecture is most commonly used for image recognition tasks?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which architecture was purpose-built to scan spatial patterns like edges and textures across a grid of pixels?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are the go-to architecture for image recognition. CNNs use convolutional layers that slide filters across images to detect features like edges, shapes, and textures. These features are combined in deeper layers to recognize complex patterns. CNNs dramatically outperform traditional methods on image tasks.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• RNNs and LSTMs are better suited for sequential data like text or time series.
  • Transformers, originally designed for NLP, are now also used successfully for vision tasks (Vision Transformers).
  • Popular CNN architectures include ResNet, VGG, and EfficientNet.

questions.title: Natural Language Processing
questions.scenario: A customer service department wants to automatically categorize incoming support tickets by topic. The tickets are written in free-form text.
questions.questionText: Which field of AI focuses on enabling computers to understand, interpret, and generate human language?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which AI discipline specifically targets the gap between how humans communicate and how machines process information?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is the AI field focused on the interaction between computers and human language. NLP tasks include text classification (categorizing tickets), sentiment analysis, named entity recognition, machine translation, and text generation. Modern NLP often uses transformer-based models like BERT and GPT.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• NLP tasks are divided into Natural Language Understanding (NLU) and Natural Language Generation (NLG).
  • AWS services like Amazon Comprehend, Amazon Lex, and Amazon Transcribe are NLP services.
  • Transformers and attention mechanisms revolutionized NLP, enabling better context understanding.

questions.title: Generative AI
questions.scenario: A marketing team wants to use AI to generate product descriptions, blog posts, and social media content based on simple prompts.
questions.questionText: What type of AI models are designed to create new content such as text, images, or code based on input prompts?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about the distinction between models that classify existing data and models that produce something new.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Generative AI refers to models that can create new content - text, images, audio, video, or code. These models learn patterns from vast amounts of training data and generate new content that follows those patterns. Large Language Models (LLMs) like those powering ChatGPT and Claude are generative AI models. AWS offers access to generative AI through Amazon Bedrock.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Foundation models are large pre-trained models that can be fine-tuned for specific tasks.
  • Discriminative models classify or predict (e.g., "Is this spam?"), while generative models create ("Write an email").
  • Prompt engineering is the practice of crafting inputs to get desired outputs from generative AI.

questions.title: Amazon Bedrock Overview
questions.scenario: A company wants to build generative AI applications using foundation models from various providers without managing infrastructure. They want to access models from Anthropic, Amazon, and others through a single API.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides access to foundation models from multiple providers through a unified API?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider which AWS service lets you call foundation models without managing any infrastructure.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed service that provides access to foundation models (FMs) from leading AI companies including Anthropic (Claude), Amazon (Titan), Meta (Llama), Cohere, Stability AI, and others through a single API. Bedrock allows you to build generative AI applications without managing infrastructure, and supports customization through fine-tuning with your own data.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Bedrock supports text generation, summarization, image generation, embeddings, and chat applications.
  • Bedrock Agents can orchestrate interactions between FMs and company data/systems.
  • Data used with Bedrock is not shared with model providers and is encrypted.

questions.title: Amazon SageMaker Purpose
questions.scenario: A data science team wants a complete platform to prepare data, build models, train them at scale, and deploy to production. They need MLOps capabilities and the ability to use their own algorithms.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides an end-to-end machine learning platform for building, training, and deploying custom models?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about which AWS service covers the full build-train-deploy pipeline with support for custom algorithms.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon SageMaker is a fully managed machine learning service that provides every component needed to build, train, and deploy ML models. It includes SageMaker Studio (IDE), Data Wrangler (data preparation), built-in algorithms, distributed training, automatic model tuning, and deployment options. SageMaker supports custom models using popular frameworks like TensorFlow, PyTorch, and scikit-learn.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• SageMaker Canvas enables no-code ML model building for business analysts.
  • SageMaker Clarify helps detect bias in data and models and explains predictions.
  • SageMaker Pipelines enables MLOps with CI/CD for machine learning.

questions.title: Amazon Rekognition
questions.scenario: A security company needs to analyze video feeds to detect people and objects. They want a pre-trained solution without building custom computer vision models.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides pre-trained computer vision capabilities for image and video analysis?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which service offers ready-to-use vision capabilities so you don't have to train your own computer vision model?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon Rekognition is a fully managed computer vision service that provides pre-trained models for analyzing images and videos. It can detect objects, scenes, faces, text, celebrities, and inappropriate content. Rekognition Video can analyze streaming video for real-time applications. No machine learning expertise is required - you simply call the API with your images or videos.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Rekognition Custom Labels allows training custom models for domain-specific object detection.
  • Face comparison can verify identity by comparing faces across images.
  • Content moderation detects unsafe or inappropriate content automatically.

questions.title: Amazon Comprehend
questions.scenario: A company receives thousands of customer reviews daily. They want to automatically determine whether each review is positive, negative, or neutral, and extract key topics mentioned.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides natural language processing to analyze text for sentiment, entities, and key phrases?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about which AWS service is purpose-built for extracting meaning, sentiment, and entities from text.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon Comprehend is a natural language processing (NLP) service that uses machine learning to find insights in text. It can perform sentiment analysis (positive/negative/neutral/mixed), entity recognition (people, places, organizations), key phrase extraction, language detection, and topic modeling. Comprehend Medical is a specialized version for healthcare text.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Comprehend Custom allows training custom classifiers and entity recognizers with your own data.
  • Comprehend Medical extracts medical information like medications, conditions, and dosages from clinical text.
  • PII detection and redaction helps protect personal information in documents.

questions.title: Amazon Transcribe
questions.scenario: A call center wants to automatically convert recorded customer calls into text transcripts for quality analysis and compliance purposes.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service converts speech to text using automatic speech recognition (ASR)?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which AWS service focuses specifically on turning spoken audio into written words?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon Transcribe is a fully managed automatic speech recognition service that converts speech to text. It supports batch transcription of audio files and real-time streaming transcription. Features include speaker identification, custom vocabularies for domain-specific terms, automatic content redaction for sensitive information, and support for multiple languages.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Amazon Transcribe Call Analytics is optimized for call center recordings with sentiment and issue detection.
  • Custom vocabularies improve accuracy for industry-specific terminology.
  • Amazon Transcribe Medical is HIPAA-eligible for healthcare transcription.

questions.title: Amazon Polly
questions.scenario: An e-learning company wants to convert their written course materials into natural-sounding audio narration for accessibility and mobile learning.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service converts text to lifelike speech?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider the opposite direction from speech-to-text — which service goes from written words to audio?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon Polly is a text-to-speech (TTS) service that uses deep learning to synthesize natural-sounding human speech. It offers dozens of lifelike voices in multiple languages. Polly supports SSML (Speech Synthesis Markup Language) for controlling aspects like pronunciation, volume, and speaking rate. Neural TTS voices provide the most natural-sounding speech.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Polly offers standard and neural voice engines, with neural providing more natural speech.
  • Brand Voice allows creating a custom voice unique to your organization.
  • Speech marks enable synchronizing speech with animations or highlighting text.

questions.title: Amazon Translate
questions.scenario: A global company needs to automatically translate customer support tickets from multiple languages into English for their support team.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides neural machine translation for text?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about which AWS service is specifically designed to convert text from one language to another.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon Translate is a neural machine translation service that delivers fast, high-quality, and affordable language translation. It supports translation between many language pairs and can automatically detect the source language. Custom Terminology ensures that specific terms (brand names, product names) are translated consistently.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Active Custom Translation allows adapting translations to match your style and terminology.
  • Translate integrates with S3 for batch translation of documents.
  • Real-time translation is available for chat applications and live content.

questions.title: Amazon Lex
questions.scenario: A company wants to build a conversational chatbot for their website that can understand natural language and guide customers through common tasks like checking order status.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service enables building conversational interfaces (chatbots) using voice and text?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which AWS service shares technology with a well-known voice assistant for building dialog-driven interfaces?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon Lex is a fully managed AI service for building conversational interfaces into applications using voice and text. Lex uses the same deep learning technologies that power Amazon Alexa. You define intents (user goals), utterances (ways to express intent), and slots (parameters). Lex handles speech recognition, natural language understanding, and dialog management.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Lex integrates with AWS Lambda for fulfillment logic and backend processing.
  • Lex V2 provides improved conversation flow management and multi-language support.
  • Amazon Connect integrates Lex for AI-powered contact center solutions.

questions.title: Amazon Textract
questions.scenario: An accounting firm needs to extract text, tables, and form data from scanned invoices and receipts to automate data entry.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service extracts text, handwriting, tables, and forms from scanned documents?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider which service goes beyond basic OCR to understand the structure of forms and tables in scanned documents.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon Textract is a machine learning service that automatically extracts text, handwriting, and data from scanned documents. Unlike simple OCR, Textract can identify and extract data from forms (key-value pairs) and tables while maintaining their structure. It processes documents like invoices, tax forms, medical records, and contracts.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Textract Queries allows asking specific questions about document content.
  • Textract Analyze Expense is optimized for processing invoices and receipts.
  • Textract Analyze ID extracts information from identity documents.

questions.title: Amazon Personalize
questions.scenario: An e-commerce platform wants to provide personalized product recommendations to each user based on their browsing and purchase history.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides real-time personalized recommendations?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about which AWS service uses the same recommendation technology behind a major e-commerce platform.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon Personalize is a fully managed ML service that makes it easy to develop applications with real-time personalized recommendations. It uses the same technology that powers Amazon.com's recommendations. You provide user interaction data, and Personalize trains custom models for use cases like product recommendations, personalized search, and customized marketing.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Personalize supports real-time recommendations that adapt to user behavior during a session.
  • Use cases include "Customers who viewed X also viewed Y" and personalized re-ranking of search results.
  • Personalize handles the entire ML pipeline: data processing, algorithm selection, training, and deployment.

questions.title: Amazon Forecast
questions.scenario: A retail company needs to predict future product demand to optimize inventory levels and reduce stockouts.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service uses machine learning to generate accurate time-series forecasts?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which AWS service is purpose-built for predicting future values from historical time-series data?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon Forecast is a fully managed service that uses machine learning to generate accurate forecasts. It's designed for time-series data and automatically examines historical data to identify patterns. Forecast can incorporate related time series (like price and promotions) and metadata (like product category) to improve accuracy. Common use cases include demand forecasting, resource planning, and financial forecasting.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Forecast uses algorithms developed at Amazon, including DeepAR+ for neural network-based forecasting.
  • It automatically handles missing values, outliers, and seasonality patterns.
  • What-if analysis allows testing different scenarios (e.g., promotional impacts).

questions.title: Amazon Kendra
questions.scenario: A large corporation wants to build an enterprise search solution that can understand natural language questions and find relevant information across multiple internal data sources.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides intelligent enterprise search powered by machine learning?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider which AWS search service understands intent behind questions rather than just matching keywords.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon Kendra is an intelligent search service powered by machine learning. Unlike keyword-based search, Kendra understands the intent behind queries and returns precise answers from unstructured data. It connects to common enterprise repositories (SharePoint, Salesforce, S3, databases) and returns specific answers, relevant documents, and FAQs ranked by relevance.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Kendra provides different response types: factoid answers, FAQ matches, and document excerpts.
  • Domain-specific models can be fine-tuned for industries like healthcare, legal, and finance.
  • Kendra integrates with generative AI through retrieval augmented generation (RAG) patterns.

questions.title: AI Bias Definition
questions.scenario: A hiring company is using an ML model to screen resumes. They notice the model consistently ranks candidates from certain demographic groups lower than others.
questions.questionText: What term describes systematic errors in AI systems that create unfair outcomes for certain groups?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: What kind of systematic problem causes a model to consistently treat certain demographic groups differently?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Bias in AI systems refers to systematic errors that create unfair outcomes for specific groups. Bias can originate from training data that underrepresents or misrepresents certain populations, from biased labeling, or from the model learning societal biases present in historical data. Detecting and mitigating bias is a crucial aspect of responsible AI development.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Types of bias include sampling bias, measurement bias, and algorithmic bias.
  • AWS SageMaker Clarify helps detect bias in data and models and explains predictions.
  • Bias metrics include demographic parity, equalized odds, and disparate impact.

questions.title: Model Explainability
questions.scenario: A bank uses an ML model to approve or deny loan applications. Regulators require the bank to explain why specific applications were denied.
questions.questionText: What responsible AI concept involves understanding and explaining how a model makes its predictions?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about what regulators demand when they ask "why did the model make this particular decision?"

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Explainability in AI refers to the ability to understand and describe how a model arrives at its predictions. For regulated industries like finance and healthcare, explainability is often required to justify decisions affecting individuals. Techniques include feature importance, SHAP values, and model-agnostic explanations. More complex models (like deep neural networks) are often harder to explain than simpler models.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• SageMaker Clarify provides feature attributions showing which inputs influenced predictions.
  • LIME and SHAP are popular techniques for explaining individual predictions.
  • There's often a tradeoff between model accuracy and interpretability.

questions.title: Data Privacy in AI
questions.scenario: A healthcare company wants to train an ML model on patient data while ensuring patient privacy is protected and compliance requirements are met.
questions.questionText: Which practice helps protect sensitive information when training AI models?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider which option directly addresses the risk of exposing individual identities in training datasets.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Protecting privacy in AI involves multiple practices: data anonymization (removing or masking PII), encryption (protecting data at rest and in transit), access controls (limiting who can access data), and differential privacy (adding noise to prevent identifying individuals). AWS provides encryption, IAM, and services like Amazon Macie for discovering sensitive data.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Differential privacy mathematically guarantees that individual records can't be identified.
  • Federated learning trains models across decentralized data without centralizing sensitive data.
  • Compliance frameworks like GDPR, HIPAA, and CCPA have specific requirements for AI systems handling personal data.

questions.title: Hallucinations in Generative AI
questions.scenario: A company is using a large language model to generate product documentation. They notice the model sometimes generates plausible-sounding but factually incorrect information.
questions.questionText: What term describes when generative AI models produce confident but incorrect or fabricated information?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about what we call it when a model confidently presents made-up information as if it were true.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Hallucination in generative AI refers to the model generating content that is factually incorrect, nonsensical, or entirely fabricated, while presenting it confidently. LLMs hallucinate because they predict probable text rather than verified facts. Mitigation strategies include retrieval augmented generation (RAG), grounding responses in source documents, and fact-checking outputs.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) grounds responses in actual documents to reduce hallucinations.
  • Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases enable RAG patterns for enterprise applications.
  • Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock can filter harmful or off-topic responses.

questions.title: Human Oversight
questions.scenario: A medical diagnosis AI system is being deployed. The hospital wants to ensure that AI recommendations are reviewed before being acted upon.
questions.questionText: What responsible AI principle ensures that humans remain in control of high-stakes AI decisions?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider which principle keeps a qualified person involved before high-stakes AI recommendations become final.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Human-in-the-loop (HITL) is a design pattern where humans maintain oversight and control over AI systems. In high-stakes domains like healthcare, finance, and criminal justice, HITL ensures that AI recommendations are reviewed by qualified humans before action. This approach combines AI efficiency with human judgment, accountability, and the ability to catch errors.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) provides workflows for human review of ML predictions.
  • HITL can be used for labeling training data, reviewing low-confidence predictions, or auditing decisions.
  • The level of human involvement should match the risk level of the application.

questions.title: ML Problem Framing
questions.scenario: A team is starting a new ML project. Before collecting data or building models, they need to clearly define what they're trying to achieve.
questions.questionText: What is the first step in the machine learning lifecycle?

choices.text: Define the business problem and success metrics

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Before touching any data or models, what foundational question must the team answer first?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: The ML lifecycle begins with problem framing: clearly defining the business problem, determining if ML is the right solution, and setting measurable success criteria. This step involves understanding stakeholder needs, defining what success looks like (accuracy thresholds, business KPIs), and ensuring the problem is well-suited for ML. Skipping this step leads to building solutions that don't address actual business needs.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Not all problems need ML - sometimes rule-based systems or simpler analytics are better.
  • Success metrics should include both ML metrics (accuracy, F1) and business metrics (revenue impact, cost savings).
  • Consider data availability, cost, timeline, and maintenance requirements when framing the problem.

questions.title: Data Preparation
questions.scenario: A data scientist has collected raw data for an ML project. The data contains missing values, inconsistent formats, and outliers that need to be addressed.
questions.questionText: What ML lifecycle phase involves cleaning, transforming, and preparing data for model training?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which lifecycle phase deals with messy real-world data before any algorithm ever sees it?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Data preparation is a critical ML lifecycle phase that includes data cleaning (handling missing values, removing duplicates), data transformation (normalization, encoding categorical variables), feature engineering (creating new features from existing data), and splitting data into training, validation, and test sets. Quality data preparation often has more impact on model performance than algorithm selection.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• SageMaker Data Wrangler provides visual tools for data preparation and transformation.
  • Common tasks include handling imbalanced classes, dealing with outliers, and feature scaling.
  • Data preparation typically consumes 60-80% of ML project time.

questions.title: Model Training
questions.scenario: A data scientist has prepared their data and is ready to build a predictive model. They need to select an algorithm and fit it to their training data.
questions.questionText: What ML lifecycle phase involves selecting algorithms, fitting them to data, and adjusting hyperparameters?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about which phase is where the algorithm actually processes data and adjusts its internal weights.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Model training is the phase where ML algorithms learn patterns from prepared data. This involves selecting appropriate algorithms (based on problem type and data characteristics), configuring hyperparameters (learning rate, tree depth, etc.), and running the training process. The algorithm adjusts its internal parameters to minimize prediction errors on the training data.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• SageMaker provides built-in algorithms, support for popular frameworks, and distributed training.
  • Hyperparameter tuning (HPO) automatically searches for optimal hyperparameter values.
  • Training can be compute-intensive - SageMaker offers managed infrastructure with GPU support.

questions.title: Model Evaluation
questions.scenario: A team has trained multiple models and needs to determine which one performs best and whether it meets business requirements before deployment.
questions.questionText: What ML lifecycle phase involves measuring model performance using metrics and test data?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which phase uses data the model has never seen to judge whether it's ready for real-world use?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Model evaluation is the phase where model performance is assessed using appropriate metrics on data the model hasn't seen during training. For classification, common metrics include accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC. For regression, metrics include MAE, MSE, and RMSE. Evaluation also checks for overfitting (performing well on training but poorly on test data) and bias.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Cross-validation provides more robust evaluation by testing on multiple data splits.
  • Confusion matrices show detailed classification performance across all classes.
  • SageMaker Experiments tracks and compares metrics across multiple training runs.

questions.title: Model Deployment
questions.scenario: A model has passed evaluation and is ready to be used by the production application to make predictions on new data.
questions.questionText: What ML lifecycle phase involves making a trained model available to serve predictions?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which phase transitions a model from the lab to a live environment where applications can call it?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Model deployment is the phase where a trained, evaluated model is made available to serve predictions in a production environment. Deployment options include real-time inference (for immediate predictions), batch transform (processing large datasets), and edge deployment (for IoT devices). SageMaker provides managed endpoints that automatically scale based on traffic.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• SageMaker endpoints support A/B testing and canary deployments for safe rollouts.
  • SageMaker Serverless Inference automatically scales to zero when not in use.
  • Model packaging (containers, formats like ONNX) ensures consistent inference across environments.

questions.title: Model Monitoring
questions.scenario: A deployed model's prediction accuracy has been declining over the past few months because customer behavior patterns have changed.
questions.questionText: What phenomenon occurs when the statistical properties of production data differ from training data, causing model performance to degrade?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider what happens when the real world changes but the model still reflects patterns from older data.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Data drift occurs when the input data distribution in production changes compared to what the model was trained on. This causes model performance to degrade because the model's learned patterns no longer match reality. Common causes include changing customer behavior, seasonal effects, or market shifts. Continuous monitoring and periodic retraining address drift.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Concept drift is when the relationship between inputs and outputs changes.
  • SageMaker Model Monitor automatically detects data drift, model quality issues, and feature attribution drift.
  • Setting up alerting and automated retraining pipelines helps maintain model performance.

questions.title: MLOps
questions.scenario: A company wants to automate their ML workflow including data processing, training, evaluation, deployment, and monitoring to enable rapid iteration and reliable production operations.
questions.questionText: What practice combines ML, DevOps, and data engineering to automate and streamline the ML lifecycle?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about which practice brings CI/CD and automation discipline specifically to the machine learning workflow.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: MLOps (Machine Learning Operations) is a set of practices that combines ML, DevOps, and data engineering to deploy and maintain ML systems reliably and efficiently. MLOps includes version control for data and models, automated pipelines for training and deployment, continuous monitoring, and reproducibility. The goal is to shorten the cycle from experimentation to production.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• SageMaker Pipelines enables CI/CD for machine learning with automated workflows.
  • Model Registry tracks model versions, approval status, and deployment history.
  • Feature Store provides a centralized repository for ML features with versioning.

questions.title: Overfitting
questions.scenario: A model achieves 99% accuracy on training data but only 65% accuracy on new, unseen test data.
questions.questionText: What problem does this model exhibit?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: When a model aces its training set but stumbles on fresh data, what problem is at work?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Overfitting occurs when a model learns the training data too well, memorizing patterns including noise rather than learning generalizable rules. The result is excellent performance on training data but poor performance on new data. Solutions include using more training data, reducing model complexity, applying regularization, using dropout (for neural networks), or early stopping.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Regularization techniques (L1, L2) penalize model complexity to prevent overfitting.
  • Cross-validation helps detect overfitting by testing on multiple data splits.
  • The bias-variance tradeoff: high variance (overfitting) vs high bias (underfitting).

questions.title: Amazon Q
questions.scenario: A company wants an AI assistant that employees can ask questions about their company's internal documents, policies, and data.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides a generative AI-powered assistant for enterprise use that can be customized with company knowledge?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which AWS service acts as a company-wide AI assistant that you can connect to internal knowledge sources?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon Q is a generative AI-powered assistant designed for business use. Amazon Q Business can be connected to enterprise data sources to answer questions, summarize content, and complete tasks based on company knowledge. Amazon Q Developer assists software developers with coding, debugging, and understanding code. Q respects existing access permissions.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Amazon Q Business connects to over 40 enterprise data sources including S3, SharePoint, Salesforce, and databases.
  • Amazon Q Developer provides code suggestions, explains code, and helps with AWS architecture.
  • Q maintains security by respecting source system permissions - users only access information they're authorized to see.

questions.title: Transfer Learning
questions.scenario: A startup has limited labeled data for their image classification task. They want to leverage a model that was pre-trained on millions of images.
questions.questionText: What technique involves using a pre-trained model as a starting point and fine-tuning it for a specific task?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider the approach that reuses an existing model's learned knowledge rather than starting from scratch.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Transfer learning leverages a model pre-trained on a large dataset and adapts it to a different but related task. Instead of training from scratch (which requires lots of data), you fine-tune the pre-trained model with your smaller dataset. This is especially powerful for deep learning where models can learn general features (edges, shapes) that transfer to new domains.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Foundation models like those in Amazon Bedrock are designed for transfer learning through fine-tuning or prompting.
  • Common approaches: freeze early layers (general features), fine-tune later layers (task-specific features).
  • SageMaker JumpStart provides pre-trained models ready for fine-tuning.

questions.title: Regression vs Classification
questions.scenario: A real estate company wants to predict the selling price of houses based on features like square footage, location, and number of bedrooms.
questions.questionText: Is this a classification or regression problem?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Is the model predicting a number on a continuous scale, or sorting items into distinct buckets?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: This is a regression problem because the target variable (house price) is a continuous numerical value. Regression models predict numbers on a continuous scale. Classification, in contrast, predicts discrete categories (e.g., "will buy" vs "won't buy"). Common regression algorithms include linear regression, decision trees, and neural networks.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Regression metrics include Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and R-squared.
  • Binary classification (2 classes) and multi-class classification (3+ classes) are both types of classification.
  • Some problems can be framed either way - predicting a price range (classification) vs exact price (regression).

questions.title: Bedrock Knowledge Bases
questions.scenario: A company wants their generative AI application to answer questions based on their proprietary documentation rather than relying solely on the foundation model's training data.
questions.questionText: What Amazon Bedrock feature enables retrieval augmented generation (RAG) by connecting foundation models to your data sources?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about which Bedrock feature lets the model pull from your own documents before generating an answer.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Knowledge Bases for Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed RAG capability. It automatically ingests your data sources (S3, web pages, databases), converts content to embeddings, stores them in a vector database, and retrieves relevant information when users ask questions. This grounds the foundation model's responses in your actual data, reducing hallucinations and providing accurate, up-to-date answers.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• RAG combines retrieval (finding relevant documents) with generation (creating responses).
  • Knowledge Bases handles chunking, embedding, and vector storage automatically.
  • Responses include citations to source documents for verifiability.

questions.title: Bedrock Guardrails
questions.scenario: A company deploying a customer-facing generative AI chatbot needs to prevent the model from generating harmful content, discussing inappropriate topics, or revealing sensitive information.
questions.questionText: Which Amazon Bedrock feature helps implement safeguards to filter harmful content and enforce content policies?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which Bedrock feature lets you define safety rules that block harmful or off-topic model output?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock enables implementing safeguards for generative AI applications. You can configure filters to block harmful content categories (violence, hate speech, sexual content), deny specific topics (competitors, off-topic subjects), filter sensitive information (PII), and define custom word filters. Guardrails work across different foundation models consistently.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Guardrails can be applied to both user inputs and model outputs.
  • Content filters have configurable strength levels to balance safety and usability.
  • Contextual grounding checks help reduce hallucinations by verifying responses against source documents.

questions.title: Bedrock Agents
questions.scenario: A company wants their generative AI assistant to not only answer questions but also take actions like looking up customer records, creating support tickets, and sending emails.
questions.questionText: Which Amazon Bedrock capability enables foundation models to complete multi-step tasks by connecting to company systems and APIs?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which Bedrock capability lets a model go beyond answering questions to actually calling APIs and executing workflows?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon Bedrock Agents enable foundation models to complete complex, multi-step tasks by dynamically calling APIs and accessing data sources. You define action groups (the capabilities available to the agent) and the agent automatically breaks down user requests, determines which actions to take, executes them in sequence, and synthesizes the results. This enables AI assistants that can actually do things, not just answer questions.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Agents use chain-of-thought reasoning to plan and execute multi-step workflows.
  • Action groups connect to Lambda functions that interface with your systems.
  • Agents can be combined with Knowledge Bases for both actions and information retrieval.

questions.title: Embeddings
questions.scenario: A semantic search application needs to find documents similar in meaning to a user's query, not just matching keywords.
questions.questionText: What numerical representation converts text into vectors that capture semantic meaning, enabling similarity comparisons?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about how you would represent text numerically so that similar meanings end up close together.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Embeddings are dense numerical vector representations of text (or other data) that capture semantic meaning. Similar concepts have similar embeddings (close in vector space). This enables semantic search where you find documents similar in meaning, not just keyword matches. Embeddings are fundamental to RAG, recommendation systems, and many NLP applications.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Amazon Titan Embeddings in Bedrock generates embeddings for text and multimodal data.
  • Vector databases (like Amazon OpenSearch Service) store and search embeddings efficiently.
  • Embedding dimensions range from hundreds to thousands, trading accuracy for storage and speed.

questions.title: Prompt Engineering
questions.scenario: A developer is getting inconsistent results from a large language model. They want to improve the quality and consistency of outputs without changing the model itself.
questions.questionText: What practice involves crafting and optimizing input text to get better outputs from generative AI models?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider the technique that improves model output by changing how you ask, not by changing the model itself.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Prompt engineering is the practice of designing and refining input prompts to get better, more consistent outputs from generative AI models. Techniques include providing clear instructions, using examples (few-shot learning), specifying output format, adding context, and using chain-of-thought prompting for complex reasoning. Good prompts dramatically improve output quality without modifying the model.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Zero-shot prompting gives instructions without examples; few-shot includes examples.
  • Chain-of-thought prompting asks the model to show reasoning steps, improving complex task performance.
  • System prompts set the context and behavior guidelines for the conversation.

questions.title: Amazon Fraud Detector
questions.scenario: An e-commerce company needs to identify potentially fraudulent transactions in real-time before processing orders.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service uses machine learning to identify potentially fraudulent online activities?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which AWS service is purpose-built for scoring transactions as potentially fraudulent in real time?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon Fraud Detector is a fully managed service that makes it easy to identify potentially fraudulent online activities such as online payment fraud, fake account creation, and account takeover. It uses ML models trained on Amazon's fraud detection expertise. You provide your data, and Fraud Detector automatically builds, trains, and deploys customized fraud detection models.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Fraud Detector provides pre-built model templates for common fraud types.
  • Models can be updated with new data to adapt to evolving fraud patterns.
  • Real-time predictions return fraud risk scores for immediate decision-making.

questions.title: Feature Store
questions.scenario: A data science team wants to share and reuse ML features across multiple models and ensure consistency between training and inference.
questions.questionText: What MLOps component provides a centralized repository for storing, sharing, and managing ML features?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about what component ensures the same engineered features are used consistently in both training and inference.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: A Feature Store is an MLOps component that provides a centralized repository for ML features. It solves problems of feature reusability (sharing across teams and models), consistency (same features for training and inference), and discoverability (finding existing features instead of recreating them). SageMaker Feature Store provides both online (low-latency) and offline (batch) feature access.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Online store provides millisecond latency for real-time inference; offline store supports batch processing.
  • Feature versioning and lineage tracking help with reproducibility and debugging.
  • Feature Store eliminates training-serving skew by ensuring consistent feature computation.

questions.title: SageMaker Clarify
questions.scenario: A financial services company needs to detect potential bias in their loan approval ML model and explain individual predictions to comply with fair lending regulations.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service helps detect bias in ML data and models and provides model explainability?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which SageMaker tool addresses both the "is this model fair?" and "why did it decide that?" questions?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon SageMaker Clarify helps detect potential bias during data preparation and after model training. It also provides model explainability by computing feature attributions that show how much each input contributed to a prediction. This helps meet regulatory requirements for explainable AI and ensures fairer ML systems. Clarify integrates with SageMaker workflows and Model Monitor.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Clarify computes bias metrics like demographic parity, disparate impact, and equalized odds.
  • SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values explain individual predictions.
  • Clarify can run bias detection on data before training and after deployment.

questions.title: Model Fine-tuning
questions.scenario: A legal firm wants to customize a foundation model to better understand legal terminology and document formats specific to their domain.
questions.questionText: What technique adapts a pre-trained foundation model using domain-specific data while preserving its general capabilities?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider the technique that specializes a general-purpose model for a specific domain without training from scratch.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Fine-tuning is the process of taking a pre-trained foundation model and further training it on domain-specific data to improve performance on particular tasks. Unlike training from scratch, fine-tuning preserves the model's general knowledge while specializing it. Amazon Bedrock offers fine-tuning for customizing foundation models with your data while keeping the customized model private.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Full fine-tuning updates all model parameters; parameter-efficient techniques (LoRA, adapters) update fewer parameters.
  • Continued pre-training exposes the model to domain text; instruction fine-tuning teaches specific behaviors.
  • Fine-tuned models in Bedrock remain private - your data is not used to train the base model.

questions.title: Tokens in LLMs
questions.scenario: A developer is working with a large language model API that charges based on tokens and has a maximum context window of 100,000 tokens.
questions.questionText: In the context of large language models, what are tokens?

choices.text: Memory units for storing model weights
The basic units of text that the model processes, typically words or subwords

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about what an LLM breaks text into before it can process anything — the smallest pieces it works with.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: In LLMs, tokens are the fundamental units of text that the model processes. A token might be a word, part of a word (subword), or a character. Tokenization converts text into these units before processing. LLM pricing is often based on tokens, and context windows (maximum input+output length) are measured in tokens. A typical rule of thumb is that 1 token is roughly 4 characters or 0.75 words in English.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Different models use different tokenizers - the same text may result in different token counts.
  • Subword tokenization (like BPE) handles rare words by breaking them into common subunits.
  • Longer context windows allow more conversation history and larger documents but increase cost.

questions.title: Amazon Augmented AI
questions.scenario: A document processing application uses ML to extract information, but needs human reviewers to verify low-confidence predictions before accepting them.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides workflows for human review of ML predictions?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which AWS service provides managed workflows for routing low-confidence ML predictions to human reviewers?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) enables human review of ML predictions. You define conditions that trigger human review (like low confidence scores), and A2I routes those predictions to human reviewers. A2I integrates with services like Textract and Rekognition, and can use private workforce, Amazon Mechanical Turk, or third-party vendors. This implements human-in-the-loop patterns efficiently.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• A2I provides worker task templates and review interfaces out of the box.
  • Custom workflows can be created for any ML application using the A2I API.
  • Results from human review can be used to improve model training data.

questions.title: Labeling Training Data
questions.scenario: A company needs to label thousands of images to train a custom image classification model, but manual labeling is time-consuming and expensive.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service helps label training data for machine learning using human workers?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider which AWS service combines human workers with active learning to create labeled datasets efficiently.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth is a data labeling service that helps build highly accurate training datasets. It provides labeling workflows for common tasks (image classification, object detection, text classification), uses human workers (private team, Mechanical Turk, or vendors), and employs active learning to reduce labeling costs by up to 70% through automated labeling of confident examples.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Ground Truth Plus is a fully managed labeling service where AWS experts manage the labeling project.
  • Active learning uses the model being trained to automatically label high-confidence examples.
  • Built-in workflows support bounding boxes, semantic segmentation, named entity recognition, and more.

questions.title: Reinforcement Learning
questions.scenario: A robotics company wants to train an AI agent to navigate a maze by learning from trial and error, receiving rewards for reaching the goal and penalties for hitting walls.
questions.questionText: Which type of machine learning involves an agent learning to make decisions by taking actions and receiving rewards or penalties?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which learning paradigm is modeled on trial and error, where an agent discovers what works by exploring?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Reinforcement learning (RL) is a type of ML where an agent learns to make decisions by interacting with an environment. The agent takes actions, receives feedback (rewards or penalties), and learns a policy that maximizes cumulative rewards over time. RL is used for robotics, game playing (like AlphaGo), recommendation systems, and autonomous vehicles.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Key RL concepts: agent, environment, state, action, reward, policy, and value function.
  • RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) is used to align LLMs with human preferences.
  • Amazon SageMaker RL provides managed infrastructure for training RL models.

questions.title: SageMaker Canvas
questions.scenario: A business analyst without coding experience wants to build ML models to predict customer churn using their company's data.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service enables business users to build ML models using a visual, no-code interface?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about which SageMaker tool lets someone build ML models through point-and-click without writing any code.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon SageMaker Canvas is a visual, no-code machine learning service that enables business analysts to build ML models and generate predictions without writing code or having ML expertise. Users upload data, Canvas automatically prepares it, trains models, and provides predictions through a point-and-click interface. Canvas also includes generative AI capabilities for data preparation and insights.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Canvas supports common prediction types: classification, regression, and time-series forecasting.
  • Ready-to-use models are available for sentiment analysis, document classification, and more.
  • Models built in Canvas can be shared with data scientists for further refinement in SageMaker Studio.

questions.title: Model Cards
questions.scenario: A company needs to document their ML model's intended use, limitations, performance metrics, and potential risks to ensure responsible deployment.
questions.questionText: What documentation artifact provides transparency about an ML model's capabilities, limitations, and appropriate use?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: What standard documentation artifact communicates a model's intended use, known limitations, and performance to stakeholders?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Model Cards are documentation artifacts that provide transparency about ML models. They typically include: model description, intended use cases, limitations and known failure modes, performance metrics across different populations, training data description, and ethical considerations. Model Cards help stakeholders understand whether a model is appropriate for their use case and what risks to consider.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• SageMaker Model Cards allow creating, editing, and viewing model documentation alongside models.
  • Model Cards should include disaggregated performance metrics showing how the model performs across different groups.
  • Foundation model providers often publish model cards describing capabilities, limitations, and safety evaluations.

questions.title: Amazon CodeWhisperer/Q Developer
questions.scenario: A software developer wants AI assistance while coding - to generate code suggestions, explain existing code, and help identify security vulnerabilities.
questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides AI-powered coding assistance with code generation, explanation, and security scanning?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which AWS service acts as an AI pair-programmer that suggests code, explains logic, and flags security issues?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Amazon Q Developer (which evolved from CodeWhisperer) is an AI-powered coding companion. It generates code suggestions based on comments and existing code, explains unfamiliar code, identifies and fixes security vulnerabilities, helps with AWS service integration, and can transform/upgrade code. It integrates with popular IDEs and supports many programming languages.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Q Developer provides reference tracking to identify suggestions similar to open-source code.
  • Security scanning detects vulnerabilities like hardcoded credentials and SQL injection.
  • Agent capabilities can implement features, generate tests, and create documentation.

questions.title: Foundation Models
questions.scenario: A company is evaluating different AI approaches. They want to understand the difference between building custom models from scratch versus using pre-built models that can be adapted for various tasks.
questions.questionText: What term describes large AI models trained on broad data that can be adapted to a wide range of downstream tasks?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about the category of models designed to be general-purpose bases that many downstream applications build upon.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Foundation models are large AI models trained on massive, diverse datasets that can be adapted to a wide range of downstream tasks through fine-tuning or prompting. Examples include GPT, Claude, and Stable Diffusion. Rather than building specialized models for each task, organizations can leverage these pre-trained foundations, customizing them for specific needs. Amazon Bedrock provides access to multiple foundation models.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Foundation models exhibit emergent capabilities - abilities not explicitly trained but arising from scale.
  • The "foundation" metaphor reflects how these models serve as a base that many applications build upon.
  • Key foundation model providers include Anthropic (Claude), Meta (Llama), Stability AI, and Amazon (Titan).
